evidence.fitness: Walked the trader's job in headless chromium at 390 px (NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/c7666914-7b3e-532d-a2b8-8bb4f48b758c/scratchpad/s1256/walk.cjs (page served from ventures/section-1256-futures-tax-calculator with python3 -m http.server)): Load an example -> net $18,250, LT $10,950, ST $7,300, blended 21.8%, tax $3,978.50 vs $5,840.00, difference $1,861.50; CSV download carries the rows and total. A retail trader gets a reasonable gain-year estimate. The CPA named above would not use it for a return: no Form 6781 line mapping (line 3/5/6/7/8/9 to Schedule D lines 4 and 11), no netting with other Schedule D gains and losses, no bracket stacking or 0% band, no NIIT threshold, and in a loss year it prints negative 'tax' figures and a carryback note that points at the wrong part of the form and omits the amount and limits; unquoted '18,250.00' style numbers (common when copying from a PDF 1099-B) silently corrupt the result.
evidence.domain: Compared with IRC 1256(a), 1212(c), 1211(b), Form 6781 (2025) and its Box D instructions, and Rev. Proc. 2025-32. Right: mark-to-market framing, 60/40 regardless of holding period, 1099-B box 11 arithmetic, which contracts qualify (futures, broad-based index options, dealer equity options, some FX) and that SPY/QQQ/single-stock options do not. Departures: the carryback election is placed in Part II (it is box D / line 6) and described without the Box D limits (eligible amount is the smaller of the loss over 1256 gains plus $3,000 or the capital loss carryover; earliest year first; capped at the carryback year's net 1256 gain and capital gain net income; may not create or increase an NOL; not for estates and trusts; claimed by Form 1045 or amended return); the tax effect is a flat marginal blend rather than stacking the 40% on ordinary income and the 60% in the 0/15/20% bands, and NIIT is applied to the whole gain instead of the excess over the 1411 threshold; loss years ignore the $3,000 limit. A practitioner would accept the gain-year saving as a rough planning number with the stated limits, not the loss-year output.

defects.what: Loss note and FAQ say the carryback election is in 'Form 6781 Part II'; Part II is straddles. The election is box D with the amount on Part I line 6, claimed by Form 1045 or amended return.

Same wrong 'Part II' reference and an unqualified 'a net 1256 loss can be carried back three years' in the visible FAQ and FAQPage JSON-LD; Box D limits (only the loss beyond 1256 gains + $3,000, earliest year first, capped at the year's net 1256 gain, no NOL, not estates/trusts) are not stated.

In a loss year the page prints 'tax at 60/40 -$2,180 / tax if all short-term -$3,200 / difference -$1,020' for a $10,000 loss, i.e. a full-rate tax benefit, though only $3,000 is deductible against ordinary income in the year (IRC 1211(b)).
Rows with more than four fields are accepted and extras dropped: unquoted '18,250.00,-1,200.00,3,400.00' is read as 18 / 250 / -1, net -$233 instead of $22,850, with no row error.
4 of 7 seeded mutations survived: no test for tab-delimited (spreadsheet paste) input, the row-length guard, the net = 0 boundary or the default rates.
An emptied rate field passes NaN; ?? does not catch NaN, so the page shows 'blended rate NaN%' and '$NaN' tax.
num() treats U+2212 minus ('−1200') and trailing-minus ('1200-') as positive; a first data row with blank boxes ('ES,,,') is taken as a header and dropped.

Tax is a flat marginal blend, not bracket stacking; NIIT toggle applies 3.8% to the whole gain rather than the excess over the IRC 1411 threshold (single $190k + $100k: exact $20,858 + $3,420 vs tool $18,600-$21,800 + $3,800). Disclosed as 'not a bracket calculation', so a scope gap, not a hidden error.
Footer boilerplate 'Not affiliated with any court, housing agency or government body' copied from another venture.

verdict: Does not meet the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 2; median 2); finished (completeness 3). The gain-year core is exact against sources the author did not write: 1099-B box 11 per account, Form 6781 lines 8/9 at 40/60, the 26.8% top blended rate, and a single-filer 2026 case stacked on Rev. Proc. 2025-32 brackets ($9,300 = $9,300). A trader-return CPA would not sign it off: the loss carryback note and FAQ send the user to Form 6781 Part II (straddles) instead of box D / line 6 and omit the Box D limits, a $10,000 loss year is shown as a -$2,180 'tax' benefit ignoring the $3,000 limit, unquoted '18,250.00' numbers silently become a -$233 net, and the marginal-rate blend can miss stacked tax by over $2,000 on a $100k gain. Four of seven seeded mutations, including removing the tab delimiter behind the advertised 'pasted spreadsheet range', left all 20 tests green.
